author: Associated Press
description:
Joe diGenova led investigation focused on intelligence assessment that Russia interfered in 2016 election

An ally of Donald Trump said on Thursday that he has resigned from his post leading a Department of Justice investigation into whether former law enforcement and intelligence officials conspired against the Republican president.

“I did in fact resign,” Joe diGenova told the Associated Press, calling it an “honor and a privilege” to serve Trump and the justice department.

Continue reading...
title: Trump ally resigns from post leading inquiry into alleged conspiracy against president

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
Median rent for one-bedroom apartment in city tops $4,495 with a national median of $1,900

San Francisco’s mayor, Daniel Lurie, declared a rent emergency on Thursday, proposing reforms aimed at curbing evictions and preventing rent spikes as the city grapples with soaring apartment prices.

The Bay Area city, home to a large number of high-earning tech workers, has long been one of the most expensive housing and rental markets in the country.

Continue reading...
title: San Francisco mayor declares rent emergency as housing costs soar

author: Raphael Boyd
description:
No 10 says 29 new trains to be built in Derby will support 350 local jobs, as well as nearly 6,000 across the UK

No 10 has announced the construction of a new fleet of battery-powered trains that will “bring faster, more reliable journeys to the north”.

The 29 new trains, which will be run by TransPennine Express, are set to be built in Alstom’s Litchurch Lane works in Derby from 2028, which the government says will support 350 local jobs, as well as nearly 6,000 across the UK.

Continue reading...
title: New battery-powered trains will ‘bring faster journeys to north’

author: Associated Press
description:
More than a dozen ex-players are suing the University of Michigan, alleging coach and staff were aware of abuse

More than a dozen former hockey players are suing the University of Michigan, alleging their coach and other staff were aware of sexual hazing that included the forced shaving of their genitals and other abuse by teammates decades ago.

“The abuse was ritualized, meticulously planned and sadistic … Enduring sexual abuse was required to be a member of the Michigan men’s ice hockey team,” attorney Michael Pitt said in a sex discrimination lawsuit filed on Wednesday in federal court in Detroit.

Continue reading...
title: Former University of Michigan hockey players say they were sexually hazed decades ago

author: Nick Visser
description:
Follow the day’s news live

Good morning

Welcome to Guardian Australia’s live news coverage for Friday.

Continue reading...
title: Australia news live: Anthony Albanese marks 25 years since September 11; aged care provider pays back thousands to residents

author: Adam Gabbatt and David Smith in Dallas, Texas
description:
Democrats are targeting Trump’s relationship with Epstein as part of strategy ahead of midterm elections

James Talarico, the Democratic candidate for Senate in Texas, accused his rival Ken Paxton of “ignoring” survivors of Jeffrey Epstein’s sexual abuse, as Democrats seek to increase pressure on Republicans ahead of November’s midterm elections.

Speaking in Dallas, where Republicans are holding a midterm convention this week, Talarico appeared alongside one of Epstein’s victims at an exhibit that featured about 3.5m pages of Department of Justice’s files related to Epstein.

Continue reading...
title: James Talarico accuses Ken Paxton of ‘ignoring’ Epstein survivors

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas
description:
Terry Strada, whose husband was killed in the attacks, says she remains hopeful for justice as a lawsuit alleging Saudi support for the hijackers moves toward trial

The leader of one group of 9/11 victims’ families says it has “taken way too long” to hold Saudi Arabia accountable for its alleged support of the terrorists who carried out the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks, whose 25th anniversary was observed across the US on Friday.

As that grim milestone approached, Terry Strada – the national chair of 9/11 Families United – said she felt as if it had “been several lifetimes” for there to be progress in the effort “to achieve a modicum of justice through our court system” in connection with the deadliest act of terror against the US.

Continue reading...
title: Victim families say it has ‘taken way too long’ to hold Saudi Arabia accountable for alleged support on 9/11

author: Associated Press
description:
Housing market has been stymied by borrowing costs, as Iran war pushed mortgage rates higher

Sales of previously occupied US homes declined in August to their slowest annual pace in more than a year as home shoppers grappled with rising mortgage rates and home prices.

Existing home sales fell 2% last month from July to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.98m units, the National Association of Realtors said on Thursday. This is the third straight monthly decline.

Continue reading...
title: US home sales slowest in more than a year as mortgage rates and prices climb

author: Robert Tait in Washington
description:
The payments amounted to 30% of each aides’ $150,000 annual salary

Donald Trump may have committed “serious” ethical violations by giving three officials including his close personal aide Natalie Harp cash gifts of $45,000 each, according to a former White House “ethics czar”, as a watchdog group called for an investigation.

The nonpartisan Campaign Legal Center filed a complaint with the US Office of Government Ethics over the US president’s handouts to a handful of staff, arguing that an investigation is “clearly warranted”.

Continue reading...
title: Trump faces growing scrutiny over ‘profoundly concerning’ cash gifts for aides including Natalie Harp

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
Steve Hilton calls department of motor vehicles a ‘bloated bureaucracy’ as he seeks to boost his longshot campaign

The longshot California gubernatorial candidate Steve Hilton pledged this week to abolish the state’s department of motor vehicles if he is elected, promising to shutter the oft-criticized department for good and set a flat $73 annual registration fee per car.

Hilton, a Trump-backed former conservative pundit running in reliably blue California, called the state’s DMV a “bloated bureaucracy”, during a Tuesday campaign event, echoing the Trump administration’s efforts to slash the federal workforce.

Continue reading...
title: California Republican vows to abolish state DMV if elected governor

author: Guardian staff
description:
Court declined to ⁠put on hold ⁠injunction preventing the USPS from tightening rules around postal voting

A US appeals court has rejected Donald Trump’s bid to impose sweeping restrictions on mail-in voting before November’s midterm elections, dealing a fresh blow to the president’s attempted crackdown.

The Boston-based first US circuit court of appeals declined to ⁠put on hold an ⁠injunction issued by a ​lower court judge last week, preventing the US Postal Service from tightening rules around postal voting.

Continue reading...
title: US appeals court rejects Trump’s bid to impose restrictions on mail-in voting before midterms

author: Lucy Campbell
description:
David Morales wins Democratic primary for Providence mayor, unseating the incumbent mayor, Brett Smiley

In the latest in a string of victories by progressives across parts of the US, the democratic socialist David Morales won the Democratic primary for mayor in Providence, Rhode Island, on Wednesday night, unseating the incumbent mayor, Brett Smiley.

The Rhode Island state representative, who was endorsed by the Vermont senator Bernie Sanders as well as the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), is now the favorite to secure the mayoralty in the deep blue city’s November general election against the Republican nominee, 77-year-old David Talan.

Continue reading...
title: Democratic socialist clinches Rhode Island nomination amid party victories

author: Maya Yang
description:
Advanced DNA testing reveals skeletal remains belong to Cindy Marcell Blizzard, who had run away from home

Skeletal remains discovered nearly 50 years ago in North Carolina have been identified as those of a 15-year-old girl who had run away from home.

On 29 December 1977, skeletal remains and clothing were discovered in a wooded area near a tire manufacturing plant in Wilson, a city approximately 40 miles east of Raleigh. After decades of DNA testing, including advances in technology, investigators identified the remains as belonging to Cindy Marcell Blizzard, a 15-year-old girl who had run away from her home in Monkton, Maryland, in the spring of 1977, the North Carolina state bureau of investigation said.

Continue reading...
title: Remains found in North Carolina in 1970s identified as 15-year-old girl

author: PA Media
description:
Emergency services dispatched to scene on Bromley High Street on Thursday afternoon

Four people have been taken to hospital after reports of a stabbing in south-east London, emergency services said.

London ambulance service was called to reports of a stabbing on Bromley High Street at 2.19pm on Thursday.

Continue reading...
title: Four people in hospital after reports of stabbing in south-east London

author: Ben Doherty
description:
The Liberal MP and former SAS soldier is under attack from One Nation after complying with a subpoena to give evidence in the failed 2022 civil case

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

“I don’t dislike Mr Roberts-Smith at all. I pity Mr Roberts-Smith. I pity this whole process. I don’t want to be here.”

Andrew Hastie was a reluctant witness in the Ben Roberts-Smith defamation case. Hastie appeared only under force of subpoena in 2022: compelled to attend court, obliged to swear an oath, and to tell “the whole truth and nothing but the truth”.

Sig
title: ‘I don’t want to be here’: Andrew Hastie was a reluctant but ‘straightforward’ witness in the Ben Roberts-Smith defamation case

author: Catie McLeod Consumer affairs reporter
description:
Exclusive: Analysis shows cost of chicken fillets, potatoes and donuts rose during supermarket giant’s three-month promotion

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Woolworths raised prices for popular items – including a 33% mark up on chicken fillets – within days of promising to freeze prices on 300 “family staples” for three months to help customers with the cost of living.

Pricing data, compiled by comparison website CW Scanner and provided to Guardian Australia, shows the supermarket chain increasing the prices of at least four key products after starting the three-month “Price Freeze” promotion on 1 May.
title: Woolworths increased prices of at least four ‘family staples’ during ‘Price Freeze’ promotion

author: Guardian staff
description:
Latest decision appears to set the stage for the state to use its old electoral maps this year

The US supreme court again rejected a push backed by Donald Trump to overhaul Missouri’s congressional maps in a bid to hand Republicans an edge in November’s midterm elections.

Its latest ruling, after days of confusion following conflicting decisions, appears to set the stage for the state to use its old electoral maps this year.

Continue reading...
title: US supreme court again rejects Missouri congressional maps redrawn to benefit Republicans in midterms

author: Keely Aouga
description:
Daniel Owen Conahan Jr’s sentence will make him the state’s 15th person executed this year

A Florida man was scheduled for execution on Thursday after being convicted of one of a series of suspected killings that became known as the Hog Trail Murders in the 1990s.

Daniel Owen Conahan Jr, 72, was sentenced to die by lethal injection for the 1996 kidnapping and strangling of Richard Allen Montgomery. Authorities found Montgomery’s mutilated body in a wooded south-west Florida area where the remains of at least six people have been found over a three-year span.

Continue reading...
title: Florida man scheduled for execution in connection to Hog Trail Murders

author: Tom Perkins
description:
Mike Rogers has also helped kill other bills that would have provided healthcare to responders and survivors

Mike Rogers, a Michigan Republican US Senate candidate, has sought in recent weeks to create controversy over old tweets his Democratic opponent, Abdul El-Sayed posted about 9/11. He has for example, falsely suggested El-Sayed, who is Muslim, said the US deserved the attack.

But, as critics have noted, Rogers has twice voted against healthcare and other benefits for 9/11 first responders and survivors, congressional records show. He has also helped kill other bills that would have provided benefits and healthcare to first responders nationwide. Rogers, a former member of Congress, is vying for Michigan’s open US Senate seat in a tight race that could decide control of Congress during the next session.
title: Republican seeking to implicate Abdul El-Sayed over 9/11 voted twice against benefits for first responders

author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
description:
Joint appeal issued by Labour MPs Gareth Snell, who voted for the bill, and Meg Hillier, who voted against

MPs who voted for and against assisted dying have urged their respective sides not to take the “extraordinary risk” of forcing through the bill using an obscure parliamentary procedure if it continues to be blocked by the Lords.

Two Labour MPs have written a warning letter to colleagues in the crucial hours before the next vote, Gareth Snell who voted in favour of the bill, alongside Meg Hillier, who voted against.

Continue reading...
title: MPs on both sides urge Commons not to take ‘extraordinary risk’ of forcing through assisted dying bill

author: Reuters
description:
Chemours, DuPont and Corteva reach settlement after lawsuits accuse companies of polluting drinking water

Chemours, DuPont and Corteva on Thursday reached a $455m settlement with ⁠North Carolina and 11 local entities over Pfas contamination claims tied to ⁠Chemours’ Fayetteville Works ⁠plant and ​other historical discharges.

Lawsuits accusing major chemical companies of polluting U.S. drinking water ⁠with toxic Pfas chemicals – a group of pollutants referred to as “forever chemicals” – have led ⁠to settlements worth billions of dollars, including one struck ​by the three companies ‌in New Jersey ‌last year.

Continue reading...
title: Chemical companies reach $455m settlement with North Carolina over ‘forever chemicals’ claims

author: Martin Belam
description:
Speaking in Dallas, the president raised ethical concerns with an apparent $1tn offer to the electorate. Plus the US citizens who are finding moving to Scotland to be an irresistible lure

Good morning. Donald Trump has pledged to pay every adult citizen in the US $5,000 if Republicans retain the House and Senate in the midterm elections. The outlandish proposal, which would cost over $1tn, immediately raised ethical concerns.

Trump made the promise during a marathon speech at the Republican midterm convention in Dallas in which he assailed Democrats as “radical”, defended his unpopular war in Iran, and urged voters to “pretend that I’m on the ballot”. Trump claimed, without evidence, that his second term had been “the most successful two years, financially and every other way, in the history of the presidency”.

Why did the Republicans hold a m
title: Trump makes highly unusual promise of $5,000 for all if Republicans win midterms | First Thing

author: Tom Ambrose
description:
Vice-president suggests payment would not go to all and would be paid for by tariff revenues despite supreme court rulings against much of Trump’s program

  • US citizens will receive $5,000 if Republicans win midterms, Trump claims

  • Sign up for the US Breaking News email

Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.

Vice-president JD Vance appeared to partially row back on Donald Trump’s outlandish claims that every adult citizen in the US would receive $5,000 if the Republicans retain the House and Senate in the midterm elections.
title: Vance appears to walk back Trump’s offer of $5,000 ‘dividend’ if Republicans win midterms – US politics live

author: Adeshola Ore
description:
The former Australian of the Year said she stood with survivors of sexual violence ‘everywhere’ and ‘no matter who they are’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Grace Tame has apologised for her comments labelling the rape of Israeli women by Hamas during the 7 October attacks as “propaganda” and “debunked”, saying her words were “misinterpreted”.

The former Australian of the Year issued the apology in an Instagram video on Thursday. The comments were made in an ABC interview about Israel and Gaza in March.

Continue reading...
title: Grace Tame apologises for comments labelling rape of Israeli women during Hamas attacks ‘propaganda’

author: Alexandra Topping Political correspondent
description:
Labelled a tourist tax, proposals would give mayors power to decide how revenue raised should be invested

Holidaymakers will face a nightly levy on hotel stays and Airbnb-style visits in England under plans ministers are due to outline to give mayors new powers.

The idea, labelled a tourist tax, was first raised by Keir Starmer’s government in November and is similar to a scheme running in Scotland. It would allow mayors to charge a fee to visitors staying overnight and decide how the revenue raised should be invested.

Continue reading...
title: Tourists in England face nightly levy on hotel and Airbnb stays under new plans

author: Andrew Sparrow
description:
The sector is concerned by reports that there won’t be a cap on the levy that can be imposed by mayors

Good morning. Last year Andy Burnham, who was then mayor of Greater Manchester, and his close friend and ally Steve Rotheram, mayor of the Liverpool city region, were urging the government to allow mayors in England to bring in what they called a visitor levy.

Burnham and Rotheram were pushing at an open door. In May this year Keir Starmer included plans for an overnight visitor levy bill in the king’s speech.

Continue reading...
title: Hospitality industry fears jobs at risk from plan to give mayors powers to impose ‘tourist tax’

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Alexander Csergo sentenced over reckless foreign interference after preparing documents for duo who approached him on LinkedIn

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A seemingly innocuous message on a social media platform has snowballed into a Sydney man being jailed for foreign interference.

Alexander Csergo, 58, was jailed for three years and six months on Thursday, after being found guilty by a jury in March of helping Chinese spies.

Continue reading...
title: Sydney man jailed for 3.5 years over fake defence reports prepared for Chinese spies

author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
description:
Australia declined to join move by UK, Canada and France in banning trade with illegal Israeli settlements

Labor party members have criticised the federal government for not following the UK, Canada and France in banning trade with Israeli settlements in the West Bank, urging Penny Wong to mount a stronger response to violence against Palestinians.

The Labor Friends of Palestine group wrote to the foreign minister on Wednesday, calling for Australia to join a coordinated approach with allied countries, in line with changes to the party’s national platform agreed in July.

Continue reading...
title: Labor friends of Palestine criticise Australia’s decision not to join sanctions on Israeli settlements in West Bank

author: Hettie O'Brien
description:
In today’s newsletter: No Bayeux ticket? Everything you need to know about the sold-out exhibition – from its epic journey to London to a Game of Thrones likeness

Good morning. If you live in the UK, you have probably heard about the Bayeux tapestry exhibition, which opens today, and you probably haven’t got a ticket. The digital queue was nine-hours long when they first went on sale in July, and the exhibition has already broken the British Museum’s record for the number of tickets sold in a single day.

Some lucky individuals, including King Charles and aspiring overlord Peter Thiel, have been treated to early previews of the medieval tapestry. Guests staying at One Aldwych, a hotel where rooms go for £1,000 a night, can partake in the
title: Thursday briefing: 68 facts about the Bayeux tapestry as it goes on display

author: Caitlin Cassidy
description:
News outlets raise alarm after being barred from media events and condemn offensive comments made by party director James Ashby

The ABC and the Guardian have called on One Nation to reverse its ban of select media outlets from press conferences amid warnings the party is practising censorship and actively avoiding public scrutiny.

On Tuesday both outlets were asked to leave a One Nation press conference in Victoria. During the event, the state’s party leader, Warren Pickering, admitted to illegal drug use and drink driving.

Continue reading...
title: The ABC and the Guardian call on One Nation to reverse media ban amid censorship concerns

author: Sarah Collard Indigenous affairs correspondent
description:
Police allege the 78-year-old sexually abused 29 children connected to the now closed Magill training centre between 1978 and 2003

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A man who had access to children in South Australia’s youth detention centre has been charged with historical sexual abuse offences dating back to 1978.

The 78-year-old from Adelaide’s western suburbs was charged with 55 offences including multiple counts of rape, unlawful sexual intercourse
title: Man charged with sexual abuse of children linked to former Adelaide youth detention centre

author: Amanda Meade
description:
FitzSimons tells court that complainant C told him Jones, who has pleaded not guilty, would touch his penis and he ‘kept pushing it away’

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Sydney Morning Herald columnist Peter FitzSimons has told the Alan Jones trial an alleged victim he spoke to in 2019 was “tearful” and sounded “emotionally traumatised” when detailing alleged assaults by the 2GB broadcaster.

The commentator and author gave evidence in the Downing Cent
title: SMH columnist Peter FitzSimons tells Alan Jones trial alleged victim was ‘revolted’ by abuse

author: Krishani Dhanji and Tom McIlroy
description:
Lambie, a veteran and Tasmanian senator, says One Nation leader is showing her ‘true colours’

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Jacqui Lambie has accused Pauline Hanson of being a “coward” for a One Nation cartoon calling the Liberal frontbencher Andrew Hastie a traitor, amid a growing spat between the One Nation leader and the former SAS captain.

Lambie, a crossbencher and army veteran, defended Hastie on Thursday, after he called on H
title: Jacqui Lambie says Pauline Hanson a ‘bloody coward’ after One Nation cartoon calling Andrew Hastie a traitor

author: Associated Press
description:
Rubio visits Ecuador and welcomes cooperation after campaign of unilateral strikes on alleged ‘narco-terrorists’

US secretary of state Marco Rubio gave new clarity on the approach toward combating drug trafficking in Latin American waters, saying the Trump administration was focused on working with allied countries and aligning with their laws but insisting the military will “still blow up ships if need be.”

The public acknowledgment of a shift in US strategy comes a year after Washington began a campaign of unilateral deadly strikes against those it calls “narco-terrorists” operating boats in international waters.

Continue reading...
title: Rubio says US will work with allies on drug-trafficking as three killed in latest boat strike

author: Lauren Gambino
description:
Helena Foulkes beats incumbent Dan McKee after criticizing handling of Providence’s Washington bridge, now expected to be completed in 2028

Rhode Island’s Dan McKee became the first sitting governor to lose a primary in nearly a decade, bested not by a more progressive challenger or a more youthful upset but by frustration over a bridge.

McKee lost his Democratic primary to Helena Foulkes, a former longtime executive with Rhode Island-based retail pharmacy CVS, the Associated Press said on Wednesday.

Continue reading...
title: Rhode Island’s Democratic governor loses primary amid anger over bridge

author: Shrai Popat in Washington and Adam Gabbatt in Dallas
description:
Senator praises ‘great friend’ Dave McCormick and says he will work with him and Trump to support steel in Pennsylvania

Democratic senator John Fetterman made a surprise virtual appearance at the Republican midterm convention, delivering a video address supporting Dave McCormick, a Republican senator in Pennsylvania.

Fetterman, who has increasingly broken with his party since his election in 2022, said he would always reject “extremes and socialism” in the video, repeating an oft-used Republican critique of the Democratic party’s increasingly popular left wing.

Continue reading...
title: Democrat John Fetterman makes surprise appearance at Republican convention
